candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - vertical accuracy of the LiDAR data
candidates.licence_attribution: Official Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform guidance.
verified_facts: Environment Agency specification requires absolute height error below ±15 cm RMSE against Ground Truth Survey.
Environment Agency expects relative/random height error to be no more than ±5 cm.
Survey-specific Ground Truth results are referenced through the Environment Agency LIDAR Capture Programme.
semantic_limits: The ±15 cm and ±5 cm figures are survey quality-control limits, not parcel-specific confidence intervals.
These limits do not identify which time-stamped survey contributed to a composite cell.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - LiDAR Composite spatial metadata GeoPackage
candidates.licence_attribution: Official Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform guidance.
verified_facts: LiDAR Composite downloads now include a spatial metadata index file in GeoPackage format.
The spatial metadata index describes the spatial location and temporal extent of raster elevation data.
Environment Agency states technical guides describe the format and attribute schema of the index files.
semantic_limits: Presence of a GeoPackage index is lineage-discovery evidence only until an exact feature match covers the parcel.
A metadata feature must not be treated as the contributing survey without spatial, temporal and identifier matching.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - projection information
candidates.licence_attribution: Official Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform guidance.
verified_facts: Environment Agency states survey data are supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid with elevations above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The LiDAR Composite is transformed using the OSTN15 geoid model.
For time-stamped and point-cloud data, the metadata catalogue must be consulted for the survey-specific geoid model; surveys after 26 August 2016 use OSGM15.
semantic_limits: Reference-system metadata does not itself validate a parcel elevation range.
Survey-specific geoid lineage remains unknown until the contributing survey metadata is matched.

candidates.name: National Polygon dataset - Technical specification
candidates.licence_attribution: Official HM Land Registry technical specification.
verified_facts: HM Land Registry states title plans and registers show the general position of boundaries unless an exact boundary has been determined.
Index polygons show indicative title location and can be the same size, larger or smaller than the title-plan extent.
The dataset can contain gaps, slivers, underlaps and technical overlaps; all index polygons are captured to British National Grid.
semantic_limits: An index polygon must not be promoted to exact legal-boundary geometry without determined-boundary evidence.
Known topology inconsistencies require fail-closed parcel matching and geometry QA.

candidates.name: Technical guidance for GML files
candidates.licence_attribution: Official HM Land Registry technical guidance.
verified_facts: HM Land Registry INSPIRE geometry is captured against British National Grid.
Mapping to web-map projections requires reprojection from British National Grid.
HM Land Registry warns projection conversion to WGS84 can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
semantic_limits: Web-map reprojection coordinates must not replace native British National Grid geometry for exact spatial gates.
The stated possible reprojection shift is a horizontal mapping issue, not LiDAR vertical error.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Ground Truth Surveys
verified_facts: Environment Agency Ground Truth surveys contain independently surveyed elevation points used to verify time-stamped LiDAR surveys.
Ground Truth points are stated as ±3 cm RMSE and include survey date, surface type, survey method, transformation and geoid metadata.
LiDAR surveys must report less than ±15 cm RMSE and 10 cm standard deviation/random error to pass quality control.
semantic_limits: Ground Truth points are survey-QC references and are not substitutes for parcel DTM cell samples.
A Ground Truth survey can support multiple LiDAR surveys, so it does not by itself establish composite contributing-survey identity.
